day_shape: 73 items: Kouhestak wedding strike fallout dominates Iranian channels with claims of US precision munitions and 13 military dead, IDF says it cleared Hezbollah's Ali al-Taher underground network, Israel freed five Lebanese detainees, Katz threatens Iran's energy infrastructure, one UK parliamentary question tabled on Iran cyber activity.

threads.label: Kouhestak wedding strike fallout
threads.summary: Iranian regime channels amplified condemnation of the US strike on a wedding in Kouhestak/Sirik, with Defa Press claiming American precision guided munitions and an F-18 were used, and IRGC commander Vahidi issuing a message to families. Tasnim reported six additional Iranian military deaths from US strikes this week, bringing the toll to at least 13, while Times of Israel noted Amman's account that IRGC missiles were intercepted or fell in remote areas.

threads.label: Ali al-Taher ridge operation
threads.summary: The IDF said it completed clearing Hezbollah's underground infrastructure on the Ali al-Taher Ridge near Nabatiyeh, describing a network built over two decades. Iranian and Lebanese regime-channel reports framed the operation as a Zionist air attack, and Jerusalem Post reported Iran warning the US of major retaliation if Israel struck Hezbollah positions on the ridge.

threads.label: Israel releases five Lebanese detainees
threads.summary: Israel's Prime Minister's Office announced the release of five Lebanese detainees arrested in recent months, framed as a gesture linked to the return of Lebanese Jewish community leaders' remains. IRIB characterised the move as Israel freeing prisoners of war in US coordination and denied any exchange was taking place.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and economic pressure
threads.summary: Defa Press and parliamentary security chair Ibrahim Azizi asserted Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz had transformed global economic conditions, while Jerusalem Post reported analysts assessing US strikes had weakened Iran's ability to mine the strait as oil flows recovered. Jerusalem Post also reported hardliner pressure to sever fibre-optic cables under the strait, and analysis of Syria as a potential US-backed energy corridor bypassing Hormuz.

threads.label: Katz threats and regime-change talk
threads.summary: Defense Minister Israel Katz warned that an Iranian attack would free the IDF from restrictions and lead it to target all regime infrastructure including energy, citing signs Iran could take desperate measures under economic pressure. Jerusalem Post reported Trump administration officials again speaking openly about the possibility of an internal uprising in Iran as US Middle East deployments were extended.

threads.label: Netanyahu October 7 timeline release
threads.summary: Israel's Prime Minister's Office released a record of Netanyahu's schedule on 7 October 2023, stating he was first informed of the Hamas attack at 6:30am. KAN and Jerusalem Post reported he did not speak with then-IDF chief Herzi Halevi until 9:45am, roughly three hours after the attacks began.

threads.label: Iran domestic strain and rights concerns
threads.summary: Iran International reported shortages of about 800 medicines with costs potentially tripling, a rights group asking German prosecutors to investigate crimes against humanity linked to 2025-26 protests, and the UN fact-finding mission urging withdrawal of a bill imposing up to 30 years' imprisonment for foreign contacts. Jerusalem Post reported Iranian university professors threatening a nationwide strike over unpaid wages.
